dynamics-split.title: Dynamics Split
dynamics-split.content:
Spontaneous breaking of a grand unified symmetry group \( G \) at high energies divides the unified force dynamics into distinct low-energy gauge sectors that evolve independently under the renormalization group. This physical transition, representing the dynamics split, governs how the single coupling constant of a unified gauge group bifurcates into the split couplings of the Standard Model group \( SU(3)_C \times SU(2)_L \times U(1)_Y \). Under the principles of Special Relativity in QFT, the local gauge fields satisfy Poincaré covariance, ensuring that the quantum transitions are invariant under Lorentz boosts and translations in the flat Minkowski spacetime. Before the unified symmetry group is broken, the action of the system is formulated on the symplectic manifold, where the classical trajectories are governed by Maupertuis\s Principle \( \delta \int \mathbf{p} \cdot d\mathbf{q} = 0 \), ensuring that the phase space path extremizes the abbreviated action functional. By evaluating these path variations, the theory establishes a continuous link between the high-energy unified dynamics and the low-energy split dynamics.

The variational structure of this symmetry-breaking dynamics is deeply connected to the path-dependent propagation of physical fields in the phase space. Under the mathematical framework of Stationary Action, the continuous time evolution of the fields before spontaneous symmetry breaking is governed by a self-adjoint Hamiltonian operator \( \hat{H} \), which generates the path of stationary phase on the symplectic manifold. This variational structure ensures that the joint wave packet propagates deterministically, carrying a local phase that is dynamically determined by the classical Lagrangian density \( \mathcal{L} \) integrated along each local path segment. The dynamics split breaks this simple variational description, introducing a split in the field coordinates where the single, unified action is replaced by a sum of independent action terms for the broken subgroups. By extremizing the action functional, the theory preserves the coherence of the fields before the transition, but this simple structure is split into distinct gauge coupling constants at lower energies.

The strong-weak coupling dualities of these split gauge groups can be analyzed using topological mappings between their respective field theories. Under the algebraic framework of S-Duality, the coupling constant \( g \) of a gauge theory is mapped to the reciprocal coupling \( 1/g \) of a dual theory, demonstrating that the strongly coupled regime of one split sector can be modeled as the weakly coupled regime of its dual. This duality mapping requires that the physical states of the broken gauge group are mapped to the topological solitonic states of the dual group, maintaining the integrity of the partition function. By evaluating these dual transitions, the theory establishes a direct connection between the algebraic structure of the split gauge groups and their non-perturbative topological properties. This non-perturbative equivalence ensures that the running of the gauge couplings under S-duality remains consistent across all scales, protecting the physical spectrum from unphysical divergence.

The spontaneous breaking of the grand unified group occurs at a characteristic energy scale where the running couplings of the Standard Model intersect. This high-energy threshold, representing the Unification Energy (The GUT Scale) \( M_{\text{GUT}} \approx 10^{16} \text{ GeV} \), serves as the mathematical boundary where the split gauge couplings contract into a single, unified coupling constant \( g_U \). Above this scale, the beta-function coefficients \( b_i \) for the individual split groups vanish, and the unified group \( SU(5) \) govern the dynamics. Below this unification threshold, the gauge couplings split and run independently, with their sloped trajectories determined by the particle content of the theory. By measuring the low-energy values of the couplings at the Z-boson mass scale \( M_Z \), physicists can extrapolate their running trajectories to high energies, verifying that supersymmetry or other new physics is required to achieve exact gauge coupling unification at the GUT scale.

The physical path traced by the gauge couplings under the renormalization group flow is resolved by extremizing the path-dependent action functional of the quantum fields. Under the mathematical framework of the Principle of Least Action, the continuous running of the coupling constants is governed by the beta functions \( \beta_i(g) \), which generate the stationary path in the coupling space \( \mathcal{C} \). This variational structure ensures that the physical couplings propagate along geodesic trajectories determined by the metric on the coupling space. The dynamics split introduces a splitting of these trajectories at the symmetry-breaking scale, where the single path splits into three independent paths representing the three Standard Model forces. By evaluating these trajectories, the theory establishes that the running of the couplings is a continuous, deterministic process governed by the local geometry of the coupling space, preserving the underlying symmetries of the unified theory.

The classical limiting case of this dynamics split is resolved at low energies where the heavy gauge bosons decouple from the active degrees of freedom, causing the running of the split coupling constants to contract into the static, classical couplings of classical electrodynamics. In this classical limit \( Q^2 \to 0 \), the quantum loop corrections to the gauge propagators vanish, and the logarithmic running of the couplings contracts into the fixed, constant charges of classical field theory. Under this continuous reduction, the renormalization group running of the split gauge couplings is mathematically formulated by the relation

\[ \frac{d\alpha_i^{-1}(t)}{dt} = -\frac{b_i}{2\pi} \]

This renormalization group equation governs the split running of the inverse gauge coupling constants \( \alpha_i^{-1}(t) \) as a function of the logarithmic energy scale \( t = \ln(Q/Q_0) \). The beta-function coefficients \( b_i \), unique to each split subgroup, dictate the sloped trajectories of the couplings below the grand unification scale. This non-unitary scaling equation illustrates how the dynamics split achieves a unified description of physical interactions, bridging the high-energy grand unified regime and the low-energy classical regime without requiring any arbitrary split in the physical laws.

informational-shift.title: Informational Shift
informational-shift.content:
Holographic transformations of quantum information content in strongly coupled field theories establish a rigorous mathematical equivalence under topological dualities. This structural mapping, defining the informational shift, describes how the Von Neumann entropy and mutual information of a subregion transform when the physical description of a field theory is mapped to its dual representation. Under the rules of Proton Decay, the transition from a baryonic state to leptonic states is mediated by high-energy virtual processes that shift the local information content of the quantum state, violating baryon number conservation. This local transition is analyzed using the algebraic framework of S-Duality, which maps a strongly coupled theory with coupling constant \( g \) to a weakly coupled dual theory with coupling \( 1/g \). This strong-weak duality maps the physical quantum states to topological solitonic states, demonstrating that the informational shift preserves the global partition function \( Z \) while reorganizing the local degrees of freedom.

The variational description of these information-preserving dualities is deeply connected to the path-dependent propagation of physical fields in the phase space. Under the mathematical framework of the Action Functional \( S[\Phi] = \int \mathcal{L} \, d^4x \), the continuous time evolution of the fields is governed by a self-adjoint Hamiltonian operator, which generates the path of stationary phase on the symplectic manifold. This variational structure ensures that the joint wave packet propagates deterministically, carrying a local phase that is dynamically determined by the classical Lagrangian density integrated along each local path segment. The informational shift under S-duality preserves this variational description, demonstrating that the action of the dual theory is physically equivalent to the action of the original theory under a non-local field redefinition. By extremizing the action functional, the theory establishes a direct connection between the algebraic Hermiticity of the field operators and the preservation of quantum entanglement entropy \( S_E \) of the density operator \( \hat{\rho} \) in holographic transitions.

The high-energy transitions that drive this informational shift are mediated by the massive gauge bosons of the unified theory. In grand unified models, the exchange of X and Y Bosons (Leptoquarks) \( X_\mu \) and \( Y_\mu \) couples quarks directly to leptons, mediating the baryon-violating transitions that shift the information content of the states. The coupling constants of these leptoquark fields scale with the grand unification scale, ensuring that the informational shift is heavily suppressed at low energies but becomes dominant at high-energy colliders or during the early universe. By evaluating these transitions, the theory establishes a direct connection between the algebraic structure of the unified gauge groups and the rate of information transfer between the quark and lepton sectors. Under this continuous monitoring, the holographic mutual information shift is formulated by the relation

\[ I(A:B) = S(\hat{\rho}_A) + S(\hat{\rho}_B) - S(\hat{\rho}_{AB}) \]

This mutual information equation dictates the informational shift as a function of the reduced density operators \( \hat{\rho}_A \) and \( \hat{\rho}_B \) for the individual subsystems \( A \) and \( B \) and their joint density operator \( \hat{\rho}_{AB} \). The mutual information \( I(A:B) \) measures the total quantum and classical correlations shared between the two subsystems, serving as a non-local metric that remains invariant under unitary dualities. This holographic correlation equation illustrates how the informational shift reorganizes the entanglement structure of the fields, demonstrating that the information content of the composite system is exactly conserved under all coordinate transformations.

The path-dependent propagation of this quantum information is analyzed by evaluating the variational properties of the classical trajectory. Under the mathematical framework of the Abbreviated Action \( W = \int \mathbf{p} \cdot d\mathbf{q} \), the path of stationary phase represents the classical trajectory of the system in the phase space coordinates \( \mathbf{q}, \mathbf{p} \), where the virtual variations of the coordinates vanish. This variational structure ensures that the propagation of the wave packet is deterministic before the measurement is performed, maintaining the causal structure of the theory under all coordinate transformations. The informational shift does not violate this causal structure, as the statistical transitions are completely determined by a self-adjoint Hamiltonian operator, preventing the propagation of superluminal signals. By evaluating the abbreviated action along the dual trajectories, the theory establishes a direct connection between the classical path and the quantum information content, demonstrating that the information is topologically protected.

The strong-weak dualities that govern this informational shift are extended to relativistic string theories using winding and momentum states. Under the principles of T-Duality, a string theory compactified on a circle of radius \( R \) is physically equivalent to a dual theory compactified on a circle of radius \( \tilde{R} = \alpha'/R \), where the momentum states of the original theory are mapped directly to the winding states of the dual theory. This winding-momentum duality maps the physical coordinates to dual coordinates, demonstrating that the informational shift under T-duality maps the short-distance quantum physics to long-distance classical physics. By requiring the partition function to be invariant under T-duality, the theory mathematically guarantees that the total information content of the string remains unchanged, protecting the vacuum from unphysical instabilities and maintaining the stability of the physical states.

The classical limiting case of this informational shift is resolved in the macroscopic limit where the Planck's constant \( \hbar \) approaches the classical limit of zero, causing the quantum entanglement entropy to contract into the classical Shannon entropy of local probability distributions. In this classical limit \( \hbar \to 0 \), the non-local quantum correlations vanish, and the quantum uncertainty relations contract into the deterministic points of classical phase space, allowing for the simultaneous measurement of all variables with arbitrary precision. Under this continuous reduction, the reduced density operator of either subsystem becomes a classical statistical mixture, and the non-local correlation functions contract into local, separable joint probability distributions. This smooth transition demonstrates that the quantum measurement backaction matches the classical statistical inference in the high-density macroscopic limit, maintaining the absolute continuity of physical principles.

null-geodesics.title: Null Geodesics
null-geodesics.content:
Trajectories of massless particles in a curved pseudo-Riemannian manifold trace out paths of vanishing spacetime interval, establishing the foundational causal structure of general relativity. These path-dependent curves, defining null geodesics, govern the propagation of light and gravitational waves through the warped geometry of spacetime characterized by the metric \( g_{\mu u} \). In the mathematical formulation of these trajectories, the equivalence of gravitational and inertial mass is quantified by The Eötvös Parameter (\(\eta\)) \( \eta = 2 rac{|a_1 - a_2|}{a_1 + a_2} \), which must vanish to satisfy the weak equivalence principle. This fundamental symmetry ensures that all massless particles follow identical null paths, regardless of their frequency or polarization. To resolve the coordinate anomalies of these trajectories in rotating reference frames, physicists analyze the relativistic rotational effects using the framework of The Ehrenfest Paradox: Rotation and Rigidity, which proves that the spatial geometry of a rotating disk is non-Euclidean, forcing light paths to deflect from flat trajectories.

The variational description of these light-like trajectories is deeply connected to the path-dependent propagation of physical states in the phase space. Under the mathematical framework of Hamilton's Principle, the continuous motion of a photon before registration is governed by a self-adjoint Hamiltonian \( H(\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{p}) \), which generates the path of stationary phase on the symplectic manifold. This variational structure ensures that the joint wave packet propagates deterministically, carrying a local phase that is dynamically determined by the classical Lagrangian density integrated along each local path segment. The null geodesics extremize this variational description, demonstrating that the photon follows a path of stationary action where the first variation of the spacetime interval \( ds^2 = 0 \) vanishes. By extremizing the action functional, the theory establishes a direct connection between the algebraic Hermiticity of the metric tensor and the physical propagation of light in a real-valued spacetime geometry.

The parallel propagation of the tangent vector along these null curves requires that the covariant derivative of the velocity vector vanishes. In this differential geometry, the Connection Coefficients \( \Gamma^\mu_{\alpha eta} \) represent the local gravitational force fields that accelerate the coordinates, determining the curvature-induced deflection of the light path. This parallel transport requires that The Invariant Inner Product \( g_{\mu u} U^\mu U^ u = 0 \) of the tangent vector \( U^\mu = dx^\mu / d\lambda \) remains constant along the entire trajectory, preserving the light-like nature of the path under all coordinate transformations. This invariant constraint mathematically guarantees that the photon's four-momentum remains null, protecting the light cone structure of the spacetime from unphysical coordinate singularites and maintaining the causal order of events.

The curvature-induced deflection of these null paths is calculated by evaluating the geodesic deviation equation between neighboring light rays. In this representation, the The Riemann Curvature Tensor \( R^\mu_{ u\alpha eta} \) represents the physical curvature of the spacetime manifold, determining the tidal forces that cause neighboring null paths to accelerate relative to one another. This curvature coupling requires that the deviation of the null geodesics is proportional to the Riemann tensor contracted with the tangent vectors of the paths. Under this continuous monitoring, the relativistic null geodesic equation is formulated by the relation

\[ rac{d^2 x^\mu}{d\lambda^2} + \Gamma^\mu_{\alpha eta} rac{dx^\alpha}{d\lambda} rac{dx^ eta}{d\lambda} = 0 \]

This null geodesic equation dictates the acceleration of the coordinate position \( x^\mu \) as a function of the affine parameter \( \lambda \). The connection coefficients \( \Gamma^\mu_{\alpha eta} \) represent the gravitational field strength, which acts to continuously bend the light path around massive stellar bodies. This geodesic equation illustrates how null paths are curved by the local spacetime geometry, proving that the deflection of light represents a rigorous geometric property of the pseudo-Riemannian manifold, maintaining the absolute continuity of physical laws across all scales.

The classical limiting case of these relativistic null geodesics is resolved in the flat spacetime limit where the metric tensor contract into the flat Minkowski metric, causing the curved light paths to contract into straight lines. In this classical limit \( g_{\mu u} o \eta_{\mu u} \), the connection coefficients vanish, and the geodesic equation contract into the simple equation of motion \( d^2 x^\mu / d\lambda^2 = 0 \), representing straight-line propagation in flat space. Under this continuous reduction, the light paths are governed by the flat wave equation of classical electrodynamics, where the wave packet propagates along straight lines with constant velocity \( c \). This smooth transition demonstrates that curved null geodesics contract into flat light paths as the mass density of the gravitational sources approaches zero, maintaining the absolute continuity of physical principles.
